### Short answer
Yes—use Firebase Storage (not Firestore). You already allow public reads under certain folders, so you can upload images there and use direct links in your email.

### Recommended now (no code/deploy changes)
- Use the existing publicly readable folder: `project-images/`
- Create a subfolder like `project-images/email/<campaign-name>/`
- Upload your PNG/JPGs via Firebase Console

Example URL format (note the URL-encoded slashes and `?alt=media`):
```text
https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/<your-bucket-name>/o/project-images%2Femail%2F<campaign-name>%2Fheader.png?alt=media
```

Your current `storage.rules` already allow:
```
// public read
match /project-images/{allPaths=**} {
  allow read: if true;
  allow write: if request.auth != null;
}
```

### Optional alternative
If you’d prefer a dedicated folder, we can add `email-assets/**` with public read in `storage.rules` and deploy. Just say the word and I’ll prep the edit; per your preference I won’t deploy without approval.

### Notes
- These links are stable and safe for email clients.
- No extra headers/CORS needed for inline images in emails.

- I checked your Firebase setup and confirmed you already have public-read Storage paths, so you can proceed immediately without any config changes.

- If you want me to upload a set for you or generate the exact URLs, send the files and the desired folder name.

### Fix your command
The error is because bash treats `<campaign>` as input redirection. Replace it with a real name and quote/escape paths with spaces.

#### From your Mac (recommended, since the images are local)
Example using rsync (preserves folder structure):
```bash
PROJECT_ID="my-film-jobs"
BUCKET="${PROJECT_ID}.appspot.com"
CAMPAIGN="promo-2025-08"   # change this
SRC="/Users/fco/Documents/fco hosted images"  # change if needed

gsutil -m rsync -r "$SRC" "gs://${BUCKET}/project-images/fco/hosted-images/${CAMPAIGN}"
```

Or using cp:
```bash
gsutil -m cp -r /Users/fco/Documents/fco\ hosted\ images/* gs://my-film-jobs.appspot.com/project-images/fco/hosted-images/promo-2025-08/
```

#### If you insist on Cloud Shell
Cloud Shell can’t see files on your Mac. First upload the folder to Cloud Shell (Upload in the Cloud Shell file browser), e.g. to `~/fco-hosted-images`, then:
```bash
CAMPAIGN="promo-2025-08"
gsutil -m rsync -r "$HOME/fco-hosted-images" "gs://my-film-jobs.appspot.com/project-images/fco/hosted-images/${CAMPAIGN}"
```

### URL format for your email
After upload, each image is directly accessible at:
```text
https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/my-film-jobs.appspot.com/o/project-images%2Ffco%2Fhosted-images%2Fpromo-2025-08%2F<filename>?alt=media
```
Replace `<filename>` and URL-encode spaces if any (e.g., `%20`). Public read is already allowed for `project-images/**`.

### Quick check
- No angle brackets in commands.
- Quote paths with spaces or escape them with backslashes.
- Prefer no spaces in filenames for cleaner URLs.

If you share the final `CAMPAIGN` name and a few filenames, I can generate the exact URLs for you.
